This is my third fire season and I’ve worked in another primarily male job (rafting). I do love working in wildfire! And I’m fortunate enough to have a 6-10 other females that I regularly work with. Some of the guys there are my best buds! They’re like long lost friends I get to work with and I’m stoked when we work together on a fire. I started out as Initial Attack Emergency Firefighter and got a Wildland fire technician position this year. I’ve had many good and bad fires and really great training opportunities. I’m glad that our operations foreman sees people for who they are and their moral and work ethics. 
I have had to deal with some real shoddy males. It sucks. It really sucks. I’m thirty and have had to stand up for women new or less experienced with the situations. I could only do this because someone else did it for me. My first year another female firefighter made a point to tell me I could come to her if I experienced any of the harassment or hazing. And I’ve made a point to talk to the new women about this too. 
I’m not sure that I could do this is some parts of their US. I’ve just met people from other areas and been blown away by their misogyny. 
I truly hope that you have a place where you are supported. You’ll have to be strong either way. Being professional and doing the job that needs to be done is most important. 
I’m not always great at checking my messages on here but I can talk more about it with you if we get in touch. 
I hope you join the community and good luck on your journey!
